chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the camel (being exchanged) for two camels, hand to hand, and on credit. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem if you specify by age, two Jadh' or two Sani.' Then he (peace be upon him) ordered me, so I struck off the word 'credit'.

key_terms.ثَنِيَّيْنِ: Two camels of a specific age category (Sani)
key_terms.جَذَعَيْنِ: Two camels of a specific age category (Jadh')

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid camel exchange involving credit (nasi'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of *Qard al-Hasan* or barter involving deferred delivery (Nasi'ah) in animal exchange, provided the specific age categories (Jadh' or Sani) are explicitly defined to avoid ambiguity (Gharar). The narrator’s action of striking out 'Nasi'ah' highlights the scholarly practice of ensuring the deferred element is either removed or precisely specified to validate the contract. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in commodity exchange to prevent disputes in trade.
